name: Frescobol Carioca
why: Linen shirts, knitted polos, swim shorts and tailored trousers in a Rio de Janeiro beach register, from a London company; the frescobol beach bats came first.
origin: Founded in London in 2013 by Harry Brantly and Max Leese, after a business selling Brazilian beach bats.
opview: “Inspired by Rio de Janeiro, we believe summer is more than a season — summering is a mindset.” — Frescobol Carioca, The Art of Summering

T-shirt.hp: DINIS COTTON-LINEN EMBROIDERED T-SHIRT (100% organic cotton)

Polo.hp: RINO COTTON POLO (95% cotton 5% cashmere, knitted)

Sweater.hp: JARDIM COTTON-CASHMERE SWEATER (crew neck, 95% cotton 5% cashmere)

notes.linen: 22 of 83 non-swim men’s styles lead with linen, and the house calls the Antonio linen shirt its bestselling house classic (seat_resort read, 7 Oct 2026).
notes.comfort: Elastic-waist travel suiting (Luan), drawstring trousers, cotton-linen jersey; the house’s own line is Move Freely.
notes.tech: 23 of 107 styles make a performance claim, all swim (quick-dry, stretch); no named supplier fibre. Thread proposed 2; ruled 2 on 7 Oct 2026.
notes.craft: Only 5 of 107 men’s clothing pages state a country, and none names a maker or a mill; the where-it-is-made story holds for the bats (Brazil) and shoes (Italy), not the clothes. Thread proposed 2; ruled 2 on 7 Oct 2026.
notes.boat: Resort stockists on three continents — Belmond, One&Only, Four Seasons, Six Senses — and linen with no visible mark; the deck is crewed.
notes.status: Sold through Bergdorf, Harrods, Le Bon Marché and a list of resort hotels; the clothes carry no mark, the stockist list does the signalling.
notes.surf: Swim is 24 of 107 styles and the brand’s story is Ipanema, but the clothes are linen and tailoring rather than boardshorts; seeded 7 Oct 2026 from the range.
notes.synth: 24 swim styles, 23 of them polyester or polyamide; outside swim no style leads with a synthetic (seat_resort read).
notes.forg: S to XXL in most styles, one length, no made-to-measure; elastic and drawstring waists forgive more than the size run suggests.
notes.dur: Fine linen and lightweight cotton-linen jersey; built for a season in the sun rather than years.
notes.fuss: Linen asks pressing or a tolerance for creases; silk and suede in the range ask more.
notes.golffice: Resort clothing with no office in it and no golf either; a leisure house.
notes.logo: No visible mark on any sampled style; the prints carry the identity.
notes.whitet: Dinis cotton-linen tee is a basic in the range at $115; not a reason to shop the house.
notes.prep: Linen and loafers at the beach club speak the register; the canon is Rio, not Nantucket.

craft_evidence.owned_d: no — none stated; bats said to be handmade in Brazil by marceneiros (not clothing, no workshop named)
craft_evidence.countries: 5% (5 of 107 clothing styles state a country: 4 swim "Made in the EU", 1 suede bomber "Made in Italy"); footwear pages say "Handcrafted in Italy"
craft_evidence.heritage: dated, not placed — "FRESCOBOL CARIOCA was founded in 2013"; 1945 Copacabana date belongs to the game, not the company
craft_evidence.reasoning: The claim about where it makes things holds for bats (handmade in Brazil) and shoes (handcrafted in Italy), not for the clothes: only 5 of 107 men's clothing pages state a country, and no page names a maker or a mill. The Antonio journal piece says the linen is woven in unnamed family-run Italian mills and sewn with flat-felled seams. A country-and-little-else house: 2 at most, 1 if the bats and shoes are set aside.
